custody.lastCoordHeading: ## D-367 — User delegation: Codex leads architecture completion with Claude

checkedAgainst: D-367 (delegation; authors and reviewers distinguished; existing process rules remain unless explicitly superseded by a reviewed decision; no fabricated agreement)
D-000 clauses 1-5 (adversarial review to consensus; three-turn termination to CONTESTED batched to the user; commit per decision)
D-056 pinned turn-2 subject dfb0c2af… gates 1-5 (gate 4: dedicated later D-000 cycle plus independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of that row; gate 5: MF-6)
D-133 (eligibility is a property; no leftover-design admission by name)

D-293 Decision 5 and D-314 items 1-3 (Class A openings are separate owner-controlled entries; DR-131/DR-133 sequence: shared gate-2 entry, fresh application-grade review of the exact final bytes, then the opening)
D-316 (form of a Class A opening: lift of an express reservation as the Product owner's act)
D-364 (a citation-refresh successor is not a gate-2 remainder)
DR-204 adjudication (a SATISFIED recorded without independent review is provenance-unlawful for that grade)
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 3 MUST-FIX, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 3 advisories. The reviewer-count question is answered in rulingOnReviewerCount and is not a finding.
summary: The direction is right and matches D-367: one genuine independent reviewer per unit, author assent recorded as assent, per-row verdicts inside integrated packages, no evidence weakening. Three defects would let a later SATISFIED be attacked on provenance or let an adopted user decision be superseded silently; each is repairable in one turn without changing the design.

mustFix.title: Reviewer independence is undefined for mixed-authorship units
mustFix.where: Decision 1 ('The other agent independently reviews the fixed bytes'), Decision 2 ('The pair can exchange authorship across bounded work packages. Codex owns integration … A material integration change receives renewed review'), Decision 3 (package-level review)
mustFix.defect: Once authorship is exchanged and the integrator edits the package, a package can contain bytes authored by both agents. The text names no rule that the independent reviewer of a unit authored none of that unit's bytes, and 'renewed review' of an integration change names no reviewer. Under D-367 ('Authors and reviewers must be distinguished') and the WORKLOG rule ('never count an author's own assessment as independent review'), a row verdict on a unit the reviewer partly wrote is not independent review.
mustFix.consequence: A SATISFIED re-record resting on such a verdict is the DR-204 class: measurements may be accurate, provenance is unlawful for the grade, and the row re-opens on audit.
mustFix.evidenceToResolve: State in Decision 1-3: (a) every reviewed unit (a row's package section, or a contract) has exactly one recorded author and its independent reviewer authored none of its bytes; (b) an integration edit by the reviewer is itself a unit whose author is the integrator and whose reviewer is the other agent, or the integration diff is reviewed by a fresh instance of either model with no session context; (c) the verdict file records, per unit, author and reviewer by name and the unit's digest.

mustFix.title: Adopted sequencing rules are superseded by implication, not by name
mustFix.where: Decision 3 ('Contract application, delegated Class A opening, and MF-6 can be recorded in one integrated act after review rather than serial cycles'); 'Problem and authority' ('a scoped successor to … D-056 eligibility 4-5's separate-cycle sequencing'); Decision 5 ('Source authority changes require explicit supersession')
mustFix.defect: The entry collapses three adopted sequences without naming the sentences it supersedes: D-056 gate 4 ('A dedicated later D-000 cycle plus independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of that row'); D-293 Decision 5 ('The D-056 Class A openings themselves are separate owner-controlled entries'); D-314 items 2 and 3 (shared gate-2 entry, then fresh application-grade review of the exact final contract bytes, then the opening). D-293/D-314 are user-made entries; D-056 is pinned by D-133. The subject's own Decision 5 forbids implicit supersession. It also does not say which content requirements survive the collapse.
mustFix.consequence: Reviewers of the first integrated package must either treat the collapse as unlawful (and REJECT) or read D-368 as silently overriding user-made entries; both outcomes cost turns and the second is the 'silent supersession' language the B1/B2 recommendations expressly rejected.
mustFix.evidenceToResolve: Add a 'Supersessions' paragraph to the Decision that (a) quotes each superseded sentence and its heading, (b) states that under D-367 the pair may amend D-293/D-314 sequencing, (c) states what survives as content: the fresh application-grade review of the exact final bytes cited by the opening, the per-row SATISFIED-GRADE verdict, D-056 gates 1-3 and D-133's property reading, D-316's form for the lift of an express reservation (recited as the owner's act under D-367), and (d) extends Reversibility to restore those sentences as governing.

mustFix.title: 'Independent adjudication' of a persistent split is an undefined operative term
mustFix.where: Decision 4 ('A persistent split is recorded CONTESTED and the pair works another surface or obtains an independent adjudication')
mustFix.defect: D-000 clause 2 makes the user the terminal adjudicator of a three-turn split. D-367 asks that the user see almost nothing. The subject introduces an adjudication path without saying who adjudicates, on what bytes, with what binding effect, and how it relates to D-000 clause 2. An operative rule with an undefined actor will itself be contested the first time it is used.
mustFix.consequence: Either every split goes to the user (defeating D-367's stated intent) or the lead's reading of 'independent adjudication' decides, which is fiat.
mustFix.evidenceToResolve: Specify: the adjudicator is a fresh instance of either model in a new Herdr pane with no session context (or a named third agent), dispatched with the frozen turn-3 subject and both frozen verdicts; its ruling binds only the surviving MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX identifiers and may not add findings; a ruling that itself returns a split is batched to the user under D-000 clause 2; the ruling file is retained and pinned like a verdict. State expressly that this amends D-000 clause 2's terminal step and that revocation restores it.

shouldFix.title: 'Contract application' is undefined for V2 design contracts and collides with freeze §7.2/§7.3 vocabulary
shouldFix.where: Decision 3 ('applied contract and digest', 'Contract application'); the companion drafts use 'On application it incorporates…'
shouldFix.defect: In this record 'apply/application' is the V1 route-A freeze motion. Every V2 design contract is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and is cited by the SATISFIED re-record rather than applied (D-013, D-015, D-056 gate 1). The subject does not say whether a V2 'application' changes binds, moves a freeze pin, or is simply the D-056 gate-1 recording.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Define the term once: for a V2 row, 'application' means the D-000 recording of the exact bytes as the row's accepted design contract at 0 blockers with application-grade acceptance (D-056 gate 1); binds stays NOTHING; no freeze or claim-register motion; the SATISFIED re-record cites that digest.

shouldFix.title: The three-exchange budget is not defined for a multi-row package
shouldFix.where: Decision 4 ('Three exchanges per decision remain the limit … New work cannot evade the limit by merely renumbering')
shouldFix.defect: With package-level review, 'per decision' is ambiguous: one budget for the package, or one per row verdict. A package whose rows split unevenly could either be forced CONTESTED as a whole by one row, or reset its budget by re-packaging the surviving rows, which is the renumbering the sentence forbids.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: State that the budget attaches to each row's verdict unit; a row that reaches three exchanges is recorded CONTESTED individually and removed from the package; the remaining rows keep their own counts and may be adopted.

shouldFix.title: Custody form of a package review is not stated
shouldFix.where: Decision 5 ('Frozen reviewed files and source digests are retained. Each adopted decision records its authority, author, reviewer verdict and hash …')
shouldFix.defect: The record's Stage A/B custody form (subject frozen at mode 0444 before dispatch; the verdict pins HEAD at open and the subject digest; a moved subject invalidates the verdict) is what makes 'fixed bytes' checkable. The subject says files are retained but not that the verdict pins them or that dispatch precedes edits.
shouldFix.evidenceToResolve: Add: the reviewed unit is frozen (0444) and digest-pinned before dispatch; the verdict records HEAD at open, every unit digest, and the exact register edit text; any byte change after dispatch is a new unit.

advisories.title: Optional second reviewer for SATISFIED-GRADE acts
advisories.note: A fresh instance of the author's model, with no session context, as a second Stage-A reviewer for SATISFIED-GRADE packages restores the 'dual ACCEPT 0/0' form at the highest grade at small cost. Not required by D-367; recorded as available.

advisories.title: Executable evidence should be mandatory for fixture corpora
advisories.note: Decision 1 says 'executable design evidence where applicable'. For any package that records fixture bytes, make a retained checker (run green at the recording commit, digest-pinned) a stated requirement; zero of the 144 retained check-* scripts targets a V2 corpus today (claude-initial-audit.md §5.1).

advisories.title: Clause 6 wording
advisories.note: 'This act changes no … row standing' is true of adoption; acts under it will. Say 'adoption of this workflow changes no standing; acts recorded under it change standing only through their own per-row verdicts and MF-6 edits.'

rationale: The proposal correctly identifies that the three-agent form is unavailable and refuses self-certification and package-wide closure. Its residual risk is provenance: the two agents will author, integrate and review overlapping bytes, and the record's only protection against a later DR-204-style re-open is a written rule that the reviewer of a unit authored none of it, plus explicit supersession of the adopted sequences it collapses. MF1-MF3 supply those rules without weakening evidence or narrowing scope; SF1-SF3 remove vocabulary and budget ambiguities that would otherwise cost review turns on the first package.

rulingOnReviewerCount.question: Does D-367 require two author-independent reviewers, or does one genuinely independent peer review suffice?
rulingOnReviewerCount.ruling: ONE genuinely independent peer review suffices. D-000 clause 1 requires adversarial review to consensus and names no reviewer count; the two-reviewer form was orchestrator-era practice (three agents), not a rule, and D-367 supplies a two-agent topology. D-056 gate 4 requires 'independent SATISFIED-GRADE review of that row', singular. A second reviewer is therefore NOT required by default once D-368 is adopted with MF1 repaired (the reviewer authored none of the unit's bytes). CLAUDE-D368-ADV-1 is optional strengthening, not a bar.
rulingOnReviewerCount.condition: The single review is independent only if MF1 holds per unit; without MF1 the count question is moot because the one review may not be independent.
rulingOnReviewerCount.finalAudit: Additional fresh reviewers for the final audit and for any CONTESTED adjudication (MF3) remain the right place for extra eyes.
